newsitem.title: UK: Tate drops on growing price worries.
newsitem.headline: Tate drops on growing price worries.

text.p: Shares in Tate & Lyle Plc dropped to their lowest level since mid-July amid continuing worries about pressure on U.S. sweetener prices, dealers said.
Some also cited concerns about the company's negotiations to sell high fructose syrup to the U.S. beverage industry.
By 1125 GMT, the shares were down 4p to 433-1/2, off the day's low of 430.
The company declined to comment on the negotiations, saying only that they have been going on for the last few weeks.
Tate & Lyle is scheduled to hold its annual meeting on Thursday.
The shares tumbled last week after NatWest downgraded the stock, saying declining sweetner prices would hit profits. They have remained under pressure on expectations of further downgrades.
Technical analyst Richard Marshall of Investment Research of Cambridge said the recent break below 450p sets the stage for the shares to fall to their next level of support at 390p.
